source.notes: Official CISCE specimen paper with answer key in one PDF. Every page footer prints 'ISC (CLASS XI) SPECIMEN QUESTION PAPER 2027' (question paper, PDF pages 1-10) or 'ISC (CLASS XI) SPECIMEN ANSWER KEY 2027' (answer key, PDF pages 11-19); examYear=2027 is the examination year the specimen is published for. It is a SPECIMEN, not a past board paper. No paper/set/series code is printed (the subject code appears only in the file name), so those fields are null. Official answers are taken only from the answer key in the same PDF, trimmed to value points. Cognitive-level tags are recorded as printed. 'page' is the physical PDF page of the question text. Computer Science Paper 1 (Theory), maximum 70. Part I (20 marks, compulsory): Questions 1 and 2. Part II (50 marks): candidates answer two of three questions in each of Section A (Q3-5, 10 marks each), Section B (Q6-8, Java programs, 10 marks each) and Section C (Q9-11, Python / trends in computing, 5 marks each). These are 'any two of three' choices, not OR pairs, so no choiceGroup is set; the sum of all entries' marks (95) therefore exceeds the 70 a candidate answers. Sub-parts with their own printed marks are separate entries; parts sharing one code listing or one figure (2(iii), 5(iii)) are kept together. Question 2(iii) prints different tags for (a) Analyse and (b) Apply, so cognitiveLevel is omitted for that entry. Java program answers were compacted (whitespace only) to fit the answer-length limit.
source.usage: Official CISCE publication, freely available on cisce.org; question text reproduced for study with attribution and a link to the original. Figures are not reproduced.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements marked, Assertion and Reason. Read the two statements carefully and choose the correct option.
Assertion: In Python, loop with the else clause executes only in the case of normal termination of the loop.
Reason: In Python, break statement in the body of the loop results in unnatural exit from the loop.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation for the Assertion.
Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation for the Assertion.
Assertion is true and Reason is false.
Both Assertion and Reason are false.

officialAnswer.text: (a) Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of the Assertion.

questions.text: State the use of Python keywords pass and continue with respect to loops.

officialAnswer.text: The statement pass does nothing but acts as a placeholder in the loop. It is a Null operation. The statement continue skips the statements in the current iteration and moves to the next iteration. It returns the control to the beginning of the loop. (½ mark each)

questions.text: Define the term conjunction in propositional logic. Give one example.

officialAnswer.text: Conjunction in propositional logic is a logical connective that combines two propositions using the word and. It is true only when both propositions are true and is represented by the symbol ∧. Ex: If, P: It is raining and Q: It is cold Then the conjunction is: P ∧ Q: It is raining and it is cold.

questions.text:
A Research Grant Committee includes a Director (D), Scientist (S), and Auditor (A). A research grant is sanctioned only if:
• The Director and either Scientist or Auditor agrees
OR
• All three agree
The inputs are:
INPUTS
D | Denotes the Director’s vote
S | Denotes the Scientist’s vote
A | Denotes the Auditor’s vote
(In all the above cases, 1 indicated YES and 0 indicates NO)
Output: X - Denotes sanction
(1 = sanctioned and 0 = not sanctioned)
Draw the truth table for the inputs and outputs given above.
Also, write the Boolean expression for X(D,S,A) with disjunctive operators for each of the false values (0’s) from the output column of the truth table.

questions.text: Explain the concept of a Half Adder in the context of binary addition. How does a Half Adder differ from a Full Adder?

officialAnswer.text: Half Adder is a combinational circuit which adds two input binary digits and outputs (SUM and CARRY). Half adders add two binary bits whereas, Full adder add three binary bits.

questions.text:
A class SpyNumGen has been defined to generate all Spy numbers between a specific range.
[A Spy number is a positive integer where the sum of its digits equals the product of its digits.]
Example: 1124 Product = 1×1×2×4 = 8
Sum = 1+1+2+4 = 8
Hence, 1124 is a Spy number
Some of the members of the class are given below:
Class name : SpyNumGen
Data members/instance variables:
start : to store the start of range
end : to store the end of range
Methods/Member functions:
SpyNumGen(int a, int b) : parameterised constructor to initialise the data members start=a and end=b
int sum_digits(int n) : returns the sum of the digits of the number ‘n’
int prod_digits(int n) : returns the product of the digits of the number ‘n’
void generate( ) : generates all Spy numbers between start and end by invoking the functions sum_digits() and prod_digits()
Specify the class SpyNumGen giving details of the constructor( ), int sum_digits(int), int prod_digits(int) and void generate( ). Define the main( ) function to create an object and call the functions accordingly to enable the task.
extractionIssues: Class-member table reproduced as 'name : description' lines.

questions.text: State one advantage and one challenge of IoT.

officialAnswer.text: Advantage of IoT is task automation. Challenge of IoT is security and privacy risk.

questions.text: Explain Natural Language Processing (NLP).

officialAnswer.text: It is a branch of AI that enables computers to understand, interpret and produce human language.

questions.text: Give one example each of non-malicious spamming and malicious spamming.

officialAnswer.text: Example of Non-malicious spamming: A renowned private bank continuing to send credit card promotional through mails. Example of Malicious spamming: A fake e-mail which claims that a package from a particular delivery company cannot be delivered to you until you download a “receipt” which would contain harmful spywares.

questions.text: What is Open-Source Software (OSS)?

officialAnswer.text: Open Source Software is a source code developed and maintained by open collaboration. These codes are freely available for use, and anyone can examine, modify and redistribute.

questions.text: Write the full form of GPL and explain its main feature.

officialAnswer.text: GPL stands for General Public Licence and as per GPL any modified or derived version of the OSS must also be released under the same GPL license. The source code must continue to remain open.
